title: Hypothesis-led split testing + fault-injection to validate model version pins
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Reduce regressions and unknown performance regressions when rolling new model revisions behind customer pins by running hypothesis-driven A/B tests and controlled fault-injection experiments during rollout windows. We want deterministic signals for latency, token cost, output-quality regressions, and degradations under partial failure so product teams can safely promote revisions.

Context: Current pin rollouts rely on traffic ramping and passive metrics. That leads to slow detection of subtle quality regressions and no automated rollback criteria for transient infra faults. This initiative pairs small-scale split tests with behavioral hypotheses (e.g., 'revision X increases 95th latency by >20% for long-seq requests') and active fault-injection (drop responses, simulate KV cache misses) to validate fallbacks and rollout gates.

Scope: Design the experiment framework, define hypothesis templates, add rollout gates (statistical thresholds + infra fault triggers), build lightweight dashboard views, author runbooks for manual/auto rollback, and pilot on 2 models (one chat-oriented, one embedder).
acceptance_criteria:
- Experiment framework that can split traffic by percentage behind a version pin (0.5% to 20%)
- Hypothesis templates created and stored in Confluence with at least 6 measurable signals (latency p50/p95, token cost, semantic eval score, error rate, fallback rate)
- Fault-injection hooks available in staging that simulate KV cache eviction and deliberate RPC timeouts documented in runbook
- Automated gate that will halt or rollback rollout when threshold exceeded (example: p95 latency increase > 25% AND semantic eval drop > 3 points)
- Dashboard panels in Grafana for the pilot models and an alerting playbook
- Pilot completed with one successful promotion and one intentional rollback to validate guardrails
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: conservative statistical thresholds reduce false positives but slow promotions; too-aggressive thresholds increase rollbacks and customer churn. We prioritize customer safety for P0 customers and faster promotion for internal experiments. Eng asked for an initial light-weight implementation that plugs into existing rollout hooks rather than rewriting the whole release path.

Decision: Implement feature-flagged experimenter service that schedules split tests per pin and emits standard metrics. Use existing rollout control plane to perform rollbacks. Fault-injection limited to private/staging and a small canary pool for Hosted API with explicit customer consent.
